notes: T18 at 6 points the Runner spent its last click removing a tag instead of running Server 7 (Loot Box, pay 2 with 4 credits) to steal the 1-advanced Freedom of Information for the win, and the Corp scored it next turn; earlier it let Server 5 score four agendas uncontested (T9-T15) and threw T14 and T16 into repeated runs on known, unbreakable Piranhas on HQ, losing cards each time.

Corp left R&D open T1 (Sericulture Expansion stolen) and later fed agendas into servers the 30+ credit Runner could already break: Hybrid Release with La Costa Grid behind one Hafrun (T13), Project Yagi-Uda in Server 6 behind one Karuna (T18) and Hybrid Release behind Diviner on T19 after Utae had broken it on T17; economy fell to 0-4 credits from T17 and it could not defend the last steals.

After an R&D dig on T3-T4 that stole Above the Law, the Runner clicked for credits every turn from T5 to T20 (reaching 64 credits) without ever playing a card from its full grip, while the Corp scored Divested Trust (T8, T9), Transport Monopoly (T13) and Divested Trust (T21) from a remote protected only by Afshar; it also made redundant HQ runs on T1 that saw Luana Campos three times.

Solid scoring plan: Megaprix scored T8 behind Eli, Seamless Launch fast-advanced Project Ingatan T10, and Ansel 1.0 held Melies City Luxury Line until it scored T15, followed by the winning Ingatan T18; the only oddities were sitting at 0 credits T8-T11 and some plain draw clicks on T6 and T16.

Won with good remote pressure (Freedom of Information T6, Post-Truth Dividend T7, Stoke the Embers T8, Tomorrow's Headline T9), but on T3 and T5 it ran R&D again into the known, unbreakable Piranhas and lost Underdome Irregulars and Docklands Pass to net damage for nothing.

On T6 the Corp used the second Ansel 1.0 install to overwrite a card in Server 1, sending Architect Deployment Test to an unprotected Archives where it was stolen T8, and Melies was stolen T7; it then spent most of the game at 0-5 credits clicking for credits (T2, T3, T5, T8, T18, T21) with a clogged hand, though the Project Ingatan scoring loop behind four ice eventually won.

Strong early accesses (Next Big Thing T1, Kingmaking T3, Oracle Thinktank T4) won the race, but from T5 to T10 it sat at 0-1 credits never playing its 5-card grip and repeatedly ran HQ through Vasilisa (T6 twice, T7 three times), stacking tags that fed the Corp's Backroom Machinations on T8.

From T1 to T5 the Runner made three or four R&D runs per turn through unbreakable Hammer, re-seeing the same top card while taking a tag each time; it then spent T6-T16 broke, clearing tags one at a time and never playing a card, while the Corp scored Divested Trust, Above the Law twice and Transport Monopoly from Server 3 uncontested.

The Corp played Neurospike on T4 for no effect (3 credits plus a click), protected R&D with only Anemone while the Runner stole Longevity Serum, Hybrid Release and two Lotus Haze from it, and from T6 sat at 0-3 credits clicking for credits (T11, T13) with no plan to rebuild.

On T1 the Corp iced the remote and HQ but left R&D open until T4, and on T2 Longevity Serum shuffled cards back into that open R&D, so Regenesis, Longevity Serum and See How They Run were stolen early; after that, Urtica Cipher traps, Saisentan and the Mitosis double install were played well to win.

Clean remote plan: Next Big Thing was advanced behind Ping and scored T4, then Embedded Reporting (T11) and Tomorrow's Headline (T13) were scored behind two ice; the oddities were using Next Big Thing on T5 to shuffle the whole hand back into R&D, and passive credit clicking on T6-T8.

On T3, with 10 credits and the Corp almost broke, the Runner played two Wildcat Strikes instead of running Server 1, and Above the Law scored next turn (another scored T7); on T10-T15 it repeatedly ran HQ through Afshar, losing 2 credits each run to re-see Government Subsidy and ZATO City Grid, and sat low on credits into Measured Response on T13; later Banner and Buzzsaw runs won the game.

The Corp held Next Big Thing and Tomorrow's Headline in an HQ guarded only by Ping (which Gauss broke for 1) instead of installing in its iced remote, and spent 14 credits on two Oppo Research plays (T3, T4) that tagged the Runner with no follow-up, then clicked for credits on T5 before losing.

On T6 the Runner accessed Prana Condenser in Server 2 and left it, then on T8 ran Server 4 into unrezzed ice, letting Prana collect counters from Saisentan and Vampyronassa, and ended the turn with 3 cards against 4 counters, a visible flatline the Corp took on T9; earlier, on T4-T6, it sent Red Team runs into Hafrun on R&D that it could not break.

Good tempo: Jailbreak multi-access stole Regenesis on T1, Longevity Serum was taken from Archives on T5, and Revolver and Shibboleth set up the T13-T14 HQ steals; it took heavy damage from two Urtica Cipher remotes on T2-T3, and T6-T7 were spent on low-value Archives runs and credit clicks.

With 13-16 credits the Corp kept agendas in an HQ defended only by Tithe and spent clicks drawing (T2, T4) rather than installing or adding ice, so Megaprix Qualifier (T2), Project Ingatan and Architect Deployment Test (T3) and a second Ingatan (T6) were all stolen from HQ via Docklands Pass.

Early HQ and R&D steals (Above the Law, Transport Monopoly, Divested Trust) and a steady Banner-through-Akhet R&D lock won, but the Runner hovered at 0-3 credits all game without playing economy, ran into Measured Response on T5 (losing four cards), and let Transport Monopoly score from Server 1 on T11 uncontested.

The Corp kept dumping agendas into an unprotected Archives: Hybrid Release via Hafrun's trash cost (T2), another Hybrid Release (T4, likely from the AU Co. top-card trash) and Project Yagi-Uda via Cultivate (T7), all stolen; it also installed Hybrid Release (T4) and Fujii (T8) behind thin ice, and on T5 it was down to clicking for credits.

A coherent plan: two Megaprix Qualifiers and two Project Ingatans were scored behind a 9-credit Ansel 1.0 that the Runner could never pass, with Ansel subroutines placing assets; the Corp ran at 0-3 credits for much of the game (T3-T5, T10, T13-T14) and leaned on campaigns, but it never exposed an agenda.

After an early R&D steal, the Runner clicked for credits from T6 to T13 (reaching 49) and never installed a breaker; with 46 credits it declined to pay 1 to pass Paywall on T12 and 3 to pass Grubber on T13, which would have reached the twice-advanced Artificial Cryptocrash that won the Corp the game next turn.
